newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares regain heights after Thursday's dip.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares regain heights after Thursday's dip.

text.p: Danish share prices set a new closing high on Friday after profit-taking ended a run of eight record-breaking sessions the day before.
"The market was particularly strengthened by the U.S. PPI figures and, as there is nothing to indicate a fall, we can continue to rise next week," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index gained 0.96 point to 127.25 in overall bourse turnover of 938 million crowns. The KFX December future rose 0.85 point to 127.25 with 15 contracts, each worth 100,000 crowns, traded.

Dealers expected financial, retail and property shares to be in the limelight next week, helped by the effect of lower than expected U.S. producer prices on bond markets and strong American retail sales.
The major banks all fared well on Friday; Den Danske Bank rose five crowns to 430 crowns, Unidanmark gained two crowns to 286 and BG Bank rose seven crowns to 249.
Novo Nordisk reaped benefits from publication of a major cost-cutting exercise which pushed its share up 13 crowns to 967 crowns. --Ole Mikkelsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969652
